episodes.210509: On March 26, 2026, a potent cold front tracked across central Indiana, interacting with a warm and unstable airmass to trigger severe storms.  Severe thunderstorms developed rapidly, producing large hail and damaging wind gusts across northern central Indiana that downed trees and power lines, leading to over 1,700 power outages as residents dealt with the abrupt onset of hazardous weather.||Significant structural damage was observed, including a destroyed pole barn and a garage roof failure in Clinton County. While the environment supported supercellular rotation and prompted numerous tornado warnings, the only severe modes were straight-line damaging winds and large hail, with reports of 1.5-inch hail in Veedersburg. The convective activity gradually weakened as it progressed south of the I-70 corridor and encountered a more stable airmass, effectively concluding the active weather event for the region.
episodes.210771: Scattered thunderstorms moved across northeast Illinois during the afternoon and evening of March 26th producing isolated large hail.
episodes.210772: Scattered thunderstorms moved across northwest Indiana during the afternoon and evening of March 26th producing isolated large hail.
episodes.210796: A weakening area of showers and thunderstorms in an environment with sufficient instability and shear continued tracking from eastern Ohio into portions of northwestern Pennsylvania during the evening hours of March 26, 2026. The environment across northwestern Pennsylvania was slightly less favorable with respect to instability closer to sunset but still retained a favorable amount of shear for strong-to-severe thunderstorms to continue for a couple of hours after sunset. These thunderstorms produced isolated instances of wind damage in western Warren County before thunderstorms weakened further below severe limits.
episodes.211146: At the surface, a cold front moved from the southern Great Lakes region to the Upper and Middle Ohio Valley during the early afternoon through late evening hours of the 26th as a low moved east-northeastward from southern Quebec to the Gulf of Saint Lawrence. Along and ahead of the front, scattered multicell and isolated supercell thunderstorms impacted northern Ohio as the storms persisted generally eastward or southeastward during the late afternoon through mid-evening hours of the 26th, amidst moderate to strong effective bulk shear and weak to moderate MUCAPE. The storms produced sporadic straight-line convective wind damage and severe hail. Two weak tornadoes occurred; one in Morrow County and the other in Knox County, where mixed layer LCL's were favorably-low and surface-based ESRH was maximized due to southwesterly low-level jet development.
episodes.211147: At the surface, a cold front moved from the southern Great Lakes region to the Upper and Middle Ohio Valley during the early afternoon through late evening hours of the 26th as a low moved east-northeastward from southern Quebec to the Gulf of Saint Lawrence. Along and ahead of the front, clusters of multicell thunderstorms persisted generally east-southeastward across Crawford County, PA during the late afternoon through early evening of the 26th, amidst weak MUCAPE and moderate to strong effective bulk shear. Isolated straight-line convective wind damage occurred in the Conneaut Lake area.
episodes.211226: A persistent, slow-moving trough remained over the American Samoa islands between March 26 and March 30. WFO American Samoa recorded a total of 5.45 inches of rainfall during this time. This led to saturated soils that triggered multiple landslides across the territory.
episodes.211319: Thunderstorms produced hail over parts of Lenawee and Monroe counties, up to 1 inch in diameter.
episodes.211849: An unseasonably warm and humid airmass developed across central Illinois on March 26, 2026, with some locations recording record high temperatures in the upper 80s and lower 90s. Dewpoints also surged into the lower 60s. As a cold front approached during the evening, scattered to widespread strong to severe storms developed along and ahead of the front, primarily in areas north of I-70. These storms produced hail as large as golf balls, as well as a few wind damage reports.
episodes.212349: A moist and unstable weather pattern affected Puerto Rico from March 24 through March 28, 2026, as a mid- to upper-level trough interacted with abundant tropical moisture and favorable upper-level dynamics. Periods of heavy showers and thunderstorms developed across the island, resulting in flooding concerns, urban and small-stream flooding, and rapid rises on rivers and streams. The threat was enhanced by strong upper-level support associated with a strengthening jet stream and persistent moisture across the region.
episodes.214623: At least two rounds of thunderstorms moved through this day, featuring both multicell clusters and supercells. One such supercell produced hail nearly 3 inches in diameter in Huntington County. Elsewhere, a number of places reported at least 1 inch hail along with instances of damaging wind. Two tornadoes were identified by NWS Storm Surveys.
episodes.214635: At least two rounds of thunderstorms moved through this day, featuring both multicell clusters and supercells. A number of places reported at least 1 inch hail along with instances of damaging wind. Hail 2 inches in diameter was reported in Henry County.

A survey of damage indicated a brief tornado was confirmed within a swath of wind damage south of Banquo. The circulation touched down just east of S 100 W35 and N of E 700 N in far southwestern Huntington county. It moved quickly southeast, causing extensive damage to a converted animal barn as well as a grain elevator on the property. Some tree damage was noted and a few projectiles were observed in 2 different roofs. The tornado cause tree damage to a residence as it crossed into Grant county. Additional tree damage was located on E 650 N, east of Indiana 9. Debris from the pole barn was found all the way through the track.
